title: Solve it together: show a shopping list
idea: GUIDED PROBLEM. Report three facts with three print lines, walked through UEPCC. The output is several lines, and their order matters.
problem: Show a shopping list with three items, one per line: milk, bread, eggs.

exercises.prompt:
PROBLEM: Show a shopping list — milk, bread, eggs — one item per line.

First, Understand. What is the OUTPUT you must produce?
options: Three lines of text: milk, bread, eggs
One line that adds them up
exercises.explanation: The output is three separate lines, one for each item. Naming the output first keeps you on track.

exercises.prompt: Still understanding. What facts (the things to show) does the problem give you?
options: The three items: milk, bread, eggs
exercises.explanation: The facts are the three items. You will print each one.

exercises.prompt: Next, Example. Work the output by hand — put the lines in the order the list should appear.
exercises.explanation: By hand, the three lines are milk, then bread, then eggs. This hand example is what you will check the code against.

exercises.prompt: Plan: to show three separate lines, you will use three separate print instructions.
exercises.explanation: One print per line. Three lines means three prints. The plan picks the tool before you code.

exercises.prompt: Which tool from Unit 1 shows one line of text?
exercises.explanation: print() shows text. You already know this tool — now you use it three times.

exercises.prompt: Now, Code. Arrange the print lines so the list comes out milk, bread, eggs.
exercises.explanation: The lines run top to bottom, so put milk first, bread next, eggs last. Code order equals output order.

exercises.prompt: Build just the first line of the list (it should show milk).
exercises.explanation: print("milk") shows the word milk on its own line. The text in quotes appears exactly.

exercises.prompt:
Check. You run the code and it shows:

milk
bread
eggs

Your hand example said milk, bread, eggs in that order. Verdict?
options: It passes — the lines match in the right order
It fails — the order is wrong
exercises.explanation: Output matches the hand example line for line, in order. That is what Check means.

exercises.prompt: What if the prints were in the order bread, eggs, milk instead? Would it still pass?
options: No — the lines would show in the wrong order
Yes — the words are the same
exercises.explanation: The computer prints in the order you write. Wrong order means the output does not match the example, so it fails.

exercises.prompt: A 'report a few facts' problem means: show some known facts as output, each on its own line.
exercises.explanation: Exactly. You take the facts the problem gives and print them in order. You just solved one with UEPCC!
